tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters...'), focuses on user-facing scenarios (silent logs, wrong hardware verdicts, pre-flight readiness), and explicitly lists many trigger contexts (Xid/ECC errors, slow training, FSx slowness, NCCL hangs, NVLink/Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure/Pending, 'is my cluster ready for a multi-day run'). It is a dense paragraph but stays within a reasonable length and is clearly scoped rather than vague.
tests.evidence: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. ... Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and focused on domain-specific, non-obvious facts (e.g., CloudTrail event name lookups, Capacity Block termination timing, Xid headline rules) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. It does not waste space on explaining what GPUs or clusters are.
tests.evidence: R3. Node identity survives replacement. A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace gives the node a new instance ID in the same instance group...

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (CloudTrail event matching, Capacity Block timing, coverage auditing) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible areas (recommendations, follow-up offers) leave room for agent judgment.
